# School of Math (SOMATH)

> SOMATH is a math school in New York City serving grades 1-12. Small classes of up to 6 students, taught by Harvard- and Kellogg-trained instructors on the Upper West Side (226 W 79th St, 1st Floor, NY 10024). Programs run on a rolling 6-month membership: enrichment for grades 1-8 (Little Newtons through Young Fermats), then test prep and advanced tracks (SHSAT, SAT Math, AP Pre-Calculus, AP Calculus AB/BC, AP Statistics). Every family starts with a free 30-minute in-person evaluation.

Contact: hello@schoolofmath.us · (646) 668-6151 · [schoolofmath.us](https://www.schoolofmath.us/)

## Core pages

- [Home](https://www.schoolofmath.us/): NYC math school for grades 1–12. Small groups of 6, Harvard- & Kellogg-trained teachers, free 60-min evaluation. Upper West Side · 226 W 79th St.
- [Math Enrichment Programs NYC](https://www.schoolofmath.us/math-enrichment-nyc): SOMATH's Upper West Side math enrichment programs for grades 1–12. Small in-person classes of 6, teacher-led, on a proprietary 24-class syllabus at every level. Includes a full comparison of enrichment vs. tutoring vs. Kumon vs. math apps.
- [Math Tutor NYC](https://www.schoolofmath.us/math-tutor-nyc): SOMATH's small-group math tutoring in NYC for grades 1–12. Upper West Side classroom, 6-student cap, real teachers, in-person only. Better than a private 1:1 math tutor for most students, at 30–50% of the cost. Compares SOMATH vs. private tutors vs. Kumon vs. Mathnasium vs. RSM vs. apps.
- [About SOMATH](https://www.schoolofmath.us/about): Meet Vivianne Wright (Harvard) and Marcelo Ambrozio (Northwestern) — the educators behind School of Math on the Upper West Side. 20 years preparing GMAT/GRE candidates for top business schools. Now teaching grades 1–12.
- [All courses](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses): Browse every SOMATH course — Little Newtons, Kid Einsteins, Young Fermats Pre-Algebra, Algebra Ignite, Geometry, Algebra II, SHSAT Prep, SAT Math, and AP Prep. Pick a day and enroll.
- [Contact](https://www.schoolofmath.us/contact): Visit School of Math at 226 West 79th Street, Upper West Side, NYC. Steps from the 1, B, C trains. Open Mon–Fri 3–10pm, Sat 10am–6pm. Call (646) 668-6151.

## Courses

- [Little Newtons (Grades 1–2) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/little-newtons): Little Newtons at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 1–2, Ages 6–8. Number sense, addition/subtraction fluency, fractions, word problems. 48 classes over 12 months. $246/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [Kid Einsteins (Grades 3–4) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/kid-einsteins): Kid Einsteins at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 3–4, Ages 8–10. Multiplication mastery, division, fractions & decimals, word problems, area & perimeter. 48 classes over 12 months. $367/month.
- [Young Fermats - Pre-Algebra (Grades 5–6) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/young-fermats-prealgebra): Young Fermats — Pre-Algebra at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 5–6, Ages 10–12. Integers, fractions, ratios, intro algebraic thinking — the foundation for everything that follows. $489/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [Young Fermats - Algebra Ignite (Grades 7–8) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/young-fermats-algebra-ignite): Young Fermats — Algebra Ignite at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 7–8, Ages 12–14. Linear equations, systems, exponents, factoring — a real Algebra I track. $489/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [Young Fermats - Geometry and Trigonometry (Grades 7–8)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/young-fermats-geometry): Young Fermats — Geometry and Trigonometry at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 7–8, Ages 12–14. Angles, triangles, Pythagorean, coordinate geometry, area & volume — a real intro to proof-style thinking. $489/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [Young Fermats - Algebra II (Grades 9–11) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/young-fermats-algebra-ii): Young Fermats — Algebra II at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 9–11, Ages 14–17. Quadratics, polynomials, radicals, exponentials, logarithms, and functions — the honors-track high school course. $489/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [AP Pre-Calculus (Grades 10–12) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/pre-calculus): AP Pre-Calculus at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 10–12. Functions, trig, sequences and series — the calculus foundations that actually matter. $800/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [AP Calculus AB/BC (Grades 11–12) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/ap-calculus): AP Calculus AB/BC at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 11–12. Limits, derivatives, integrals, series — aligned to your child's school syllabus with free-response drills. $800/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [AP Statistics (Grades 10–12) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/ap-statistics): AP Statistics at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 10–12. Exploring data, sampling and experimentation, probability, and statistical inference — aligned to the College Board syllabus with free-response drills. $800/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [SAT Math (Grades 9–11) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/sat-math): SAT Math at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 9–11, High School. Heart of Algebra · Problem Solving & Data · Passport to Advanced Math · Additional Topics. $640/month, $99 one-time registration.
- [SHSAT Prep (Grades 7–8) | School of Math](https://www.schoolofmath.us/courses/shsat-prep): SHSAT Prep at SOMATH on the Upper West Side — Grades 7–8, Middle School. Specialized HS Admissions math — question families, timing, scratch-paper strategy. $587/month, $99 one-time registration.

## Featured

- [Pre-Algebra Class 11 — Variables and Algebraic Expressions: Translating Words (8 SOMATH Posters, Theory & 40 Practice Questions)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/pre-algebra-class-11-variables-algebraic-expressions-translating-words): The whole grade 5–6 unit on translating words into algebraic expressions, on one page. Eight illustrated SOMATH posters walk students through variables vs constants (letters like x, y, n stand for unknown or changing numbers; constants are fixed), translating addition words (sum, plus, more than, increased by, added to, the total of → +; addition is commutative so order doesn't matter), translating subtraction words (minus, difference of, decreased by, less than, fewer than, subtracted from → −; the critical order-flip trap that "5 less than n" is n − 5 not 5 − n, and "2 subtracted from z" is z − 2 not 2 − z), translating multiplication words (product, times, twice, double, triple, four times, of → ×; the coefficient goes in front of the variable, so 3 · x is written 3x), translating division words (quotient, divided by, ratio, per, per each, out of, one-half of, one-third of → written as a fraction with whatever is named first on top), translating multi-step phrases (read one operation at a time, circle the key words, honor the order-flippers), using parentheses ("the sum of", "the difference of", "the quantity", "the total of" group two things together, so "twice the sum of x and 4" is 2(x + 4) not 2x + 4), and putting it all together as complete translations ("five less than twice a number" is 2x − 5, "half the difference of a number and 4" is (1/2)(x − 4)). Under each poster: full theory notes plus 5 practice questions with click-to-reveal step-by-step solutions — 40 questions total. Grades 5–6. Class 11 of the SOMATH Young Fermats — Pre-Algebra 48-class rolling syllabus. Upper West Side NYC.
- [Kid Einsteins Class 11 — Adding Fractions with Like Denominators (8 SOMATH Posters, Theory & 40 Practice Questions)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/kid-einsteins-class-11-adding-fractions-like-denominators): The whole grade 3–4 unit on adding fractions with like denominators, on one page. Eight SOMATH posters walk kids through what a fraction is (equal parts of a whole), numerator vs denominator (top counts parts we have, bottom counts equal parts in the whole), identifying like denominators (same bottom number = same-sized pieces = safe to add), adding the numerators when the denominators match, keeping the denominator the same, adding with fraction-strip / area models, adding on a 0-to-1 number line by making equal jumps, and translating word problems (Maya ate 2/6 + Noah ate 3/6 = 5/6 of the chocolate bar). Under each poster: full theory plus 5 practice questions with click-to-reveal solutions — 40 total. Common-mistake callouts (never add the denominators). Grades 3–4. Class 11 of the SOMATH Kid Einsteins 48-class rolling syllabus.
- [SOMATH on Fox News America Reports — Homeschooling Soars in New York City and State (Sept 14, 2026)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/homeschooling-nyc-fox-news-2026-vivianne-wright): SOMATH cofounder Vivianne Wright and Upper West Side mother Adrienne Jensen appeared on Fox News America Reports on September 14, 2026 in the segment "Homeschooling reportedly soars in New York City and state." This post embeds the segment, summarizes the underlying data (53,905 homeschooled students in NY state 2025–26, 14,000+ in NYC, +200% over 15 years, +8% since 2023, NY 2nd nationally after DC per the Empire Center, +324% NYC district-level growth), pulls together the five most-cited parent reasons (class-size rigor, low state-exam pass rates in 906 of NYC's 1,500+ schools, cost per student, time and freedom, fit for accelerated learners), and explains exactly how SOMATH supports NYC homeschool families with an in-person math track (grades 1–12, IHIP-ready quarterly progress reports, small groups of 4–8, written diagnostic, SHSAT/SAT/AP feeder ladder) from 226 W 79th St on the Upper West Side. Includes a 7-question FAQ on NYS homeschooling requirements.
- [Kid Einsteins Class 14 — Area, Perimeter & Word Problems (8 SOMATH Posters, Theory & 40 Practice Questions)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/kid-einsteins-class-14-area-perimeter-word-problems): The whole grade 3–4 area, perimeter, and word-problems unit on one page. Eight SOMATH posters walk kids through perimeter (add every side), area of a rectangle (length × width), the difference between regular length units and squared area units, area of a square, composite (L- and T-shaped) figures, finding a missing side from a known perimeter or area, real-life fence-vs-paint word-problem cues (fence/ribbon/border/trim = perimeter; paint/carpet/tile/grass = area), and the same-perimeter-different-area comparison that shows why the most square-shaped rectangle holds the most area. Under each poster: full theory plus 5 practice questions with click-to-reveal solutions — 40 total. Grades 3–4. Class 14 of the SOMATH Kid Einsteins 48-class rolling syllabus.
- [Algebra 1 Class 11 — Polynomials: Adding, Subtracting, Multiplying (10 SOMATH Posters, Theory & 50 Practice Questions)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/algebra-ignite-class-11-polynomials-add-subtract-multiply): The whole Algebra 1 polynomial-operations unit on one page. Ten SOMATH posters walk grades 7–8 through what a polynomial is, identifying terms/coefficients/constants, classifying (monomial, binomial, trinomial), degree, combining like terms, adding, subtracting, multiplying monomials (xᵐ·xⁿ = x^{m+n}), monomial × polynomial with the distributive property, and FOIL for two binomials. Under each poster: full theory expanded from the poster plus 5 practice questions with click-to-reveal step-by-step solutions — 50 total. Grades 7–8. Class 11 of the SOMATH Young Fermats — Algebra Ignite 48-class rolling syllabus.
- [The 24 Greatest Mathematicians of All Time — And How Each of Them Learned to Love Math (SOMATH essay)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/greatest-mathematicians-of-all-time): SOMATH story-essay about the 24 mathematicians history remembers as the greatest — Euclid, Archimedes, Fibonacci, Copernicus, Kepler, Descartes, Newton, Leibniz, Euler, Lagrange, Gauss, Riemann, Cantor, Hilbert, Emmy Noether, Alan Turing, Kolmogorov, von Neumann, Gödel, Ramanujan, Hadamard, Olga Taussky-Todd, Maryam Mirzakhani, and Terence Tao — and, for each one, the specific moment or mentor that made them fall in love with math. Closes on SOMATH’s teaching thesis: none of them were born loving math; they were shown it in the right way at the right moment, and that is teachable.
- [Imperial System vs Metric System — 7 Conversions Every Student Should Know (Grades 4–8 reference)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/imperial-vs-metric-7-conversions): One printable SOMATH chart with the seven imperial↔metric conversions students meet the most — 1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 foot = 30.48 cm, 1 yard = 0.914 m, 1 mile = 1.609 km, 1 gallon = 3.7854 L, 1 ounce (weight) = 28.35 g, and 1 pound = 453.6 g — with worked examples per unit, mental-math shortcuts (miles ×1.6 to km, pounds ÷2.2 to kg, etc.), and the two pitfalls the chart doesn’t warn about (U.S. vs. U.K. gallons; weight ounces vs. fluid ounces). Grades 4–8 / middle-school math / SAT & ACT prep reference.
- [Little Newtons Class 11 — Needs vs. Wants and Saving in a Piggy Bank (Grades 1–2 financial literacy)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/needs-wants-saving-little-newtons): The whole Class 11 financial-literacy foundation on one page. Eight illustrated SOMATH posters — what money is, needs vs. wants, earn/spend/save/share, what a piggy bank is (deposit, withdrawal, savings), saving over time to reach a goal, counting coins and dollars (penny, nickel, dime, quarter), the 3-jar system (Save · Spend · Share), and everyday money decisions. Under each poster: theory drawn from the poster plus 5 practice questions with click-to-reveal explanations (40 total). Grades 1–2.
- [AP Statistics Class 11 — Random Variables & Expected Value (12 SOMATH Posters, Theory & 60 Practice Questions)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/ap-statistics-class-11-random-variables-expected-value): The entire AP Statistics random-variables unit on one page. Twelve SOMATH posters walk through random variables, discrete vs. continuous, probability distributions and their validity rules, missing probabilities, expected value, interpreting E(X), games and decisions, variance, standard deviation, transforming random variables, and combining random variables. Under each poster: full theory notes plus 5 practice questions with click-to-reveal solutions (60 total). Grades 10–12.
- [Pre-Algebra in 6 Concepts — Whole Numbers, Operations, Properties, Factors, Integers & Equivalent Fractions](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/pre-algebra-6-foundational-concepts): The whole pre-algebra foundation on one page. Six SOMATH posters, full theory notes, and 60 practice questions with click-to-reveal solutions. Free class-pack PDF and teacher answer-key PDF included. Grades 5–8.
- [Homeschooling in NYC — How SOMATH Supports Homeschool Families with Math (New York Post, Sept 9 2026)](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/homeschooling-nyc-math-support-somath): SOMATH cofounder Vivianne Wright and daughter Violetta featured in the New York Post. In-person homeschool math track for grades 1–12 with IHIP-ready quarterly progress reports, small groups of 4–8, morning/midday slots, from 226 W 79th St on the Upper West Side.
